To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) control constraints, particularly actuator impairment, can lead to loss of control; (2) safe set theory can be applied to the design of envelope protection; (3) the optimal safety critical controls for envelope protection can be computed analytically; (4) the safe sets can be computed using level set methods; (5) the safe sets for the full longitudinal dynamics are four dimensional and difficult to visualize, but they can be computed and used to design control laws.
1) The ability of a pilot to maneuver an aircraft is not simply determined by its static stability.
the safe set for maneuverability can be computed using a Hamiltonian and level sets and that it can be used to assess the maneuverability and envelope protection capabilities of aircraft.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the design of control laws that can be used to protect aircraft against loss of control.
the design of control laws that prevent aircraft loss-of-control.
the development of a framework to assess and improve maneuverability, envelope protection, and flight safety.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ability to maneuver an aircraft within the envelope of safe flight is not a trivial task.
there are no general rules for maneuvering an aircraft in the presence of actuator impairment.
the ability of the pilot to maneuver the aircraft is a function of the aircraft, the flight regime, and the pilot's ability to control the aircraft.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the safe sets are not as simple as the ones for the two dimensional case.
safe sets are a useful concept in the analysis of maneuvering performance and envelope protection, and can be computed efficiently for conventional longitudinal aircraft dynamics.

the ability of a pilot to maneuver the aircraft is a complex function of both the aircraft dynamics and the pilot's control inputs and that the presence of constraints can dramatically alter the aircraft's ability to maneuver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability of a system to maneuver is not a binary yes/no question.
the safe set can be computed and used for design of envelope protective systems, and that the optimal control for safety can be computed analytically and numerically.
envelope protection systems should be based on a combination of control constraints and the ability of the pilot to maneuver around a steady state.
